results.title: Myrus Apacible on healing and returning to the spotlight: 'It’s an emotional ride'
results.description: After honing his craft through singing competitions and bar gigs, Myrus Apacible made his mark on the OPM scene as a finalist in the 2013 Philpop competition with his song "Sana Pinatay Mo Na Lang Ako," performed by Kimpoy Feliciano. Seeking to reach a wider audience, Myrus took a leap of faith and joined the second season of GMA’s singing competition “The Clash,” where he advanced to the Top 16. Things took a turn, however, when Myrus had to deal with a mental health crisis. According to Myrus, it took him six years to recover. "I was able to survive dun sa napagdaanan ko, nagtreatment ako pero matagal siya. Almost six years yung battle ko, but you know God is good and ibinalik Niya ako sa pangarap ko," Myrus told us during a press conference. As he enters a new chapter in his career, Myrus is returning to what matters most: performing. The singer-songwriter will make his comeback with “Myrus, My Time,” a concert set for October 9, 2026, at the Music Museum. According to Myrus, preparing for the concert is like an "emotional ride." "Kasi ikukwento ko dun yung naging journey ko for the past 15 years and even yung mga pinagdaanan ko, and yung pagbabalik ko sa music," Myrus shared. Myrus will also feature special guests at his concert. "Yung mga nakasama ko before, like yung vocal trio ko sa ibang bansa makakasama ko sila dito," he shared. When asked what made him decide to return to performing, Myrus simply answered that it felt like a calling. "When I released 'Hindi na Babalik' last year, parang naging calling ko siya; ni-release ko siya without expecting anything," He said. To his surprise, the song got a million views after only a month. It became his motivation. "Nung nilabas ko yung sabi ko, 10k views okay na ako, but it went viral, and the rest is history. Siguro manifestation worked na rin," he concluded.
